task.title: Page finite recurrences sparsely by status through the CLI
task.objective: Complete issue https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/999 by exposing bounded recurrence status scans as deterministic read-only JSON.
acceptance_criteria: Validate exact status, positive at-most-1024 scan size, and optional exact recurrence-ID cursor before storage access.
Emit complete matching recurrences and the kernel-owned nullable last-inspected continuation cursor.
Open existing storage read-only and fail without partial stdout on selected-window corruption or storage errors.

attempts.diagnostic: The CLI rejected recurrence status-page because the subcommand did not exist.
attempts.patch: Added CLI tests for sparse continuation, validation, exact JSON, storage absence, and selected-window corruption isolation.

attempts.summary: Implemented and refactored the read-only adapter.
attempts.diagnostic: Implemented shared status parsing, pre-storage size and cursor validation, read-only kernel delegation, and compact continuation JSON.
attempts.patch: Implemented issue 999 in crates/vela-dev/src/lib.rs with CLI tests, ADR-0098, and scheduler documentation; independent review found no blocking issue.

attempts.diagnostic: A rate-limited false green was excluded; after cooldown, CodeRabbit command 732a0b3a completed on exact head 075e226 with no actionable comments and zero unresolved threads.
attempts.patch: Kept auto-merge disabled until genuine review and the exact-head Rust gate both succeeded.

outcome.summary: Issue 999 exposed bounded sparse recurrence status paging while preserving kernel validation and cursor semantics.

verification.command: GitHub Rust quality gate for pull request 1000 exact head 075e226de62e3ee69ec3ce5a27b7d1d9acbd78e4

lessons: The CLI should parse persisted-status vocabulary once and delegate sparse selection rather than reconstructing kernel policy.
Nullable next_after reports inspected scan progress independently from result density.
The adapter adds no global discovery, ambient clock, persisted cursor, lifecycle mutation, dispatch, permission, or execution authority.
